h1:
First Time in Uttaradit
What to Know + a Trip Plan
intro: Uttaradit is a town most people only pass through on the way north, but stop and explore and you'll find the legendary town of Laplae, the largest earth-fill dam in Thailand, and local food that's hard to find anywhere else. If this is your first trip, here's what to know before you go, plus a 2-day, 1-night plan you can actually follow.
chips: 🍃 Khao Pan Phak, a true local dish

blocks.html: Uttaradit sits on the seam between the upper central plains and the north. Most people know it as the town of Laplae and as the hometown of Phraya Phichai of the Broken Sword. It isn't big and it isn't crowded, and that's exactly its charm. Come for the first time with the right prep and you'll have an easygoing trip with no one to elbow for space.

The easiest option for first-timers is the northern railway line. Uttaradit's station is a Class 1 station right in town, and nearly every Bangkok–Chiang Mai service stops here. The trip takes about 7–9 hours from Bangkok, with fares from roughly 230 THB for third class up to air-conditioned sleepers in the low thousands. Buses run from Mo Chit daily, and driving yourself along the Asia Highway (Routes 11/12) is straightforward too.

items: Train — arrive at Uttaradit station in the town center; easy to continue from there, ideal if you don't have a car
Bus — from Mo Chit to the Uttaradit bus terminal, several runs a day
Driving — the most flexible, since the sights are spread across several districts; best if you plan to reach Sirikit Dam or Laplae

blocks.title: Getting around town
blocks.html: Uttaradit doesn't have the kind of public transport you'd find in a big city. If you arrive by train and want to see Laplae and the dam, renting a car or motorbike in town is the way to go, since the main sights are 10–60 km apart.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Uttaradit trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Uttaradit
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: Uttaradit works year-round, but each season has its own feel. If you like cool, comfortable weather, come from late in the year into early the next. If you're here for the fruit, you'll want the rainy mid-year months.

items: November–February — cool and comfortable, great for walking around Laplae and heading up into the hills; clear skies and good photos
May–August — durian season for the Long Laplae and Lin Laplae varieties, plus langsat and longkong, the province's signature fruit; orchards open for tasting
March–April — central-plains hot; still doable but skip walking in the midday sun and lean on temples and cafes

blocks.title: Local fruit
blocks.html: Long Laplae and Lin Laplae are durian varieties that grow especially well around Laplae — dry flesh, small seeds, high price, and limited supply. They only appear mid-year, so if you arrive in season, count yourself lucky.
Uttaradit has local dishes you won't easily find elsewhere, especially Laplae's khao pan phak and mee pan. Work your way through these.

items.name: Khao Pan Phak
items.blurb: Freshly steamed rice-flour sheets wrapped around vegetables, egg, and meat, served with a well-balanced dipping sauce. It's a Laplae snack that families have made for generations — soft, easy to keep eating.

items.name: Mee Pan
items.blurb: A rice cracker wrapped around boldly seasoned noodles — sour and spicy from lime and chili flakes. It's a cousin of khao pan phak that Laplae locals eat alongside it.

items.name: Khao Kaep
items.blurb: Thin flour sheets dried in the sun, then grilled or eaten fresh — an old Laplae craft. Easy to pick up as a souvenir to take home.

items.name: Long Laplae & Lin Laplae durian
items.blurb: Local durian varieties with fine, dry flesh and small seeds — sweet and rich. They appear mid-year and run pricey, but worth it if you get the real thing straight from the orchard.

items.name: Laplae langsat & longkong
items.blurb: The province's signature fruit — small, sweet with a hint of tart. There's an annual festival when the fruit comes in, and they're a popular souvenir to carry home.

items.name: Kuay teow ho / made-to-order spots in town
items.blurb: In town you'll find noodle shops and rice-and-curry stalls at easy prices, open morning to evening — good for a proper meal before or after heading out of town.

blocks.text: The main sights you can't miss

items.name: Laplae Town Gate
items.blurb: The symbol of Laplae, built in an applied Sukhothai style, with a widow statue tied to the legend of a town where lying was forbidden. It's the first check-in spot in Laplae.

items.name: Mae Phun Waterfall
items.blurb: A limestone waterfall that cascades down in tiers. It's been shaped a bit by hand, but it's pretty and shallow enough to splash around — shady and good for a midday break.

items.name: Sirikit Dam
items.blurb: The largest earth-fill dam in Thailand, in Tha Pla district, with viewpoints over a reservoir that stretches to the horizon, pretty gardens, and a fish sanctuary.

items.name: Phraya Phichai Monument
items.blurb: In front of the provincial hall in the town center, honoring the hero who's a fixture of Uttaradit. It's an easy starting point for exploring the town on foot.

items.name: Wat Phra Thaen Sila At
items.blurb: Home to the Phra Thaen Sila At, a sacred object of the province, with a local museum to wander through. Good for temple and history fans.

items.name: Laplae Museum
items.blurb: Recreates old Laplae life — the rice barns, the post-birth confinement traditions, the lullabies — and helps the town's legend make a lot more sense.

blocks.html: This plan is built for first-timers who want it all — Laplae town, the local food, and some nature — without rushing. Adjust the timing to your train schedule or when you reach town.

items.activity: Arrive in Uttaradit, drop your things at a hotel in town
items.note: If you take an overnight train, you'll arrive in the morning right on time

items.activity: Stop at the Phraya Phichai Monument in front of the provincial hall
items.note: Take photos and get a quick feel for the town's history

items.activity: Drive to Laplae district, starting at the Laplae Town Gate
items.note: About 8 km from town; see the widow statue and the town legend

items.activity: Eat khao pan phak and mee pan at a Laplae shop
items.note: Signature dishes worth trying from your very first meal
Understand local life and where the town's name comes from

items.activity: Head to Mae Phun Waterfall, splash in the shallows, relax
items.note: Shady and pleasant, good for cooling off in the afternoon

items.activity: Head back into town, find dinner, and rest
items.note: The town has made-to-order spots and dessert stalls open in the evening

items.activity: Set off for Sirikit Dam in Tha Pla district
items.note: About 60 km from town, so allow time for the drive

items.activity: Take in the reservoir views, Sumalai Garden, and the dam crest
items.note: A wide-open photo spot stretching to the horizon, with great air

items.activity: Have lunch around Tha Pla, then start heading back
items.note: There are waterside restaurants to choose from

items.activity: Stop at Wat Phra Thaen Sila At on the way back
items.note: Pay your respects and walk through the local museum

items.activity: Buy souvenirs — khao kaep, and langsat–longkong in season
Head back to the train station or bus terminal for the trip home
items.note: Aim to reach the station at least 30 minutes before your service

blocks.title: If you only have one day
blocks.html: Drop Sirikit Dam and focus on Laplae town — the gate, the museum, khao pan phak, and Mae Phun Waterfall — and you'll get the full Laplae feel in a single day.

blocks.text: Things to know before you go

items: Bring cash — many local shops and orchards still mainly take cash
Plan your transport — sights are spread across several districts, so without your own car, rent one or hire a driver for the day
Check the fruit season — to taste real Laplae durian or longkong, you need to come mid-year
Book lodging ahead — there aren't many hotels in town, and they fill up fast during the fruit festival and long weekends

faq.q: How many days do I need in Uttaradit for a first trip?
faq.a: 2 days and 1 night is about right for first-timers — you get Laplae town, the local food, and Sirikit Dam. If you only have one day, focus on Laplae town and Mae Phun Waterfall.

faq.q: What's the most convenient way to get to Uttaradit?
faq.a: The northern railway line is the most convenient if you don't have a car, since the station is in the town center and nearly every Bangkok–Chiang Mai service stops here. The trip takes about 7–9 hours from Bangkok.

faq.q: What food do I have to try in Uttaradit?
faq.a: Laplae's khao pan phak and mee pan are the local specialties to try, plus khao kaep as a souvenir. And if you come mid-year, try the Long Laplae durian and Laplae longkong.

faq.q: Is it hard to get around to the sights?
faq.a: The main sights are spread across several districts, 10–60 km apart, and there isn't much public transport in town. If you arrive by train, renting a car or motorbike is the way to go.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Uttaradit?
faq.a: Late in the year into early the next is cool and comfortable for sightseeing, while mid-year is durian and Laplae longkong season — perfect for fruit lovers who want to taste the local favorites straight from the orchard.
